subject: Deployment access models and encryption roles — VPC / on-prem follow-up
messages:
From: James McCoy <james.mccoy@astrahealth.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on access & encryption for private deployment

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our InfoSec team is reviewing the technical annex for the private deployment. A few items we need clarity on before we move to procurement: 

1) Key custody model — we want to ensure our encryption keys remain under our control. Can you confirm if Redwood ever has direct access to customer-managed keys for a VPC/on-prem deployment?

2) Operator maintenance access — in the event of an emergency patch or troubleshooting session, what exactly can Redwood engineers access inside the customer environment (logs, runtime memory, model files)? Is that access auditable and time-limited?

3) Subprocessors & data flows — we need a current list of subprocessors that could touch telemetry or diagnostic data for the private deployment and the regions where backups or metrics might be exported.

We'd prefer short, concrete bullets we can paste into our procurement checklist. Attaching the draft DPA Annex we received — can you review and propose language where needed?

Best,
James McCoy
Head of Information Security
AstraHealth

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions on access & encryption for private deployment

James —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers you can use in procurement; I attached a short access matrix and a proposed Annex A wording (draft). If you want, we can convert the bullets into one-paragraph DPA language.

1) Key custody model:
- Customer-managed keys (CMK) are supported via standard KMS integrations (KMIP for HSMs or cloud KMS for cloud-hosted HSM).
- For VPC and on-prem packages Redwood does not hold key material by default. Keys remain in your control and are used via an integration endpoint in your network.
- The only exception is if the customer requests temporary operator-assisted decryption (see Operator Maintenance Access below); this requires signed change control and explicit authorization.

2) Operator maintenance access:
- Routine ops: Redwood engineers have no persistent shell or direct file-level access to customer model/data directories.
- Breakglass (emergency) access: possible only under a documented ticket, with customer approval, a strict time window, and session recording. Access is limited to the minimum required actions and recorded to your audit log endpoint.
- All maintenance sessions are logged and exported to the customer's audit target (S3/GCS endpoint in customer account or syslog collector in VPC).

3) Subprocessors & data flows:
- Subprocessors that may receive non-identifying telemetry (metrics, scheduling data): our orchestration infra partner and a metrics SaaS provider. They never receive model inputs/outputs for private deployments unless explicitly configured by customer.
- Backups or metric exports are only written to customer-controlled storage endpoints unless a customer opts into Redwood-managed retention for convenience (rare).

I attached the access matrix that maps these statements to contract language. Happy to iterate.

-r

--
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, that helps. A couple of short follow-ups so we can finalize our checklist: 

- For the KMIP/HSM integration, do you support a split-custody workflow (i.e., key activation requires a customer token + Redwood operator action), or is it strictly customer-only activation?
- On subprocessors: can you provide names/locations and a commitment window to notify us before adding any new subprocessor (we prefer 30 days)?
- On logs: you say session recordings can be exported to our syslog/S3. Can you confirm the retention minimums Redwood keeps on its side (if any) for those session recordings and for any debug artifacts that might get pulled for analysis?

If you prefer, we can schedule 30 minutes with your security engineer.

-James

James — looping in Vivek (security lead) and Neha (legal) so they can confirm the technical and contractual commitments below. Quick answers up front, then Vivek adds a technical note.

- Split-custody / activation: We support customer-only activation as the default. Split-custody workflows can be implemented via a two-party activation where the CMK requires a customer HSM trigger plus a Redwood service token for certain planned maintenance actions. That approach adds operational complexity and needs to be agreed in the onboarding runbook.

- Subprocessors: We maintain a current subprocessor registry and will commit to 30 days notice for new subprocessors that could touch telemetry or diagnostics. Current names: Orchestrix Inc. (US), MetricHub Ltd. (EU). Neither receives PII or model IO for private deployments unless you opt in.

- Session recordings & debug artifacts: By default session recordings initiated during breakglass are streamed to the customer's audit endpoint and Redwood retains only an operational digest for 7 days to support post-mortem (digest contains no model inputs/outputs). Full session artifacts are not retained by Redwood unless explicitly authorized in writing.

Neha, Vivek — can you confirm we can offer the following DPA Annex clause in our next revision (language attached as rdw-dpa-annexA-proposed-text-v1.docx):
- Customer maintains exclusive custody of CMKs; Redwood accesses key material only via customer-controlled KMS API endpoints and never exports key material out of the customer environment.
- Operator access is time-boxed, auditable, and requires customer approval for each session; session recordings are delivered to customer audit targets.

Thanks —
Rachel

--
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

James / Rachel / team —

Quick technical note on the access model and keys so procurement has the exact assurances: 

1) Key operations and activation:
- Customer-managed KMS (on-prem HSM or cloud KMS): Redwood only performs cryptographic operations over an RPC to your KMS endpoint — we never persist raw key material in our environment.
- For a split-custody activation pattern we implement a transaction workflow where the customer issues an ephemeral activation token (valid for a short window) and Redwood provides a correlated operation token; both are required to perform the change. All tokens are one-time use and logged.

2) Runtime memory and model artifacts:
- Model weights and token caches are stored in customer-controlled storage or ephemeral runtime instances that are wiped after the session. No persistent copy is transferred to Redwood-managed storage in standard configurations.
- In rare diagnostic sessions an engineer may request a memory snapshot; this must be authorized in the change control ticket and is only transferred to a customer-designated endpoint.

3) Audit & retention specifics:
- Session recordings forwarded to customer S3/GCS are retained in the customer's account per their retention policy. Redwood retains an operational digest for 7 days (metadata only).
- Debug artifacts that are handed to Redwood for analysis are retained only as agreed in the ticket; default retention on Redwood side is 0 days unless customer explicitly approves storage.

4) Network & backup considerations:
- Backups are written only to storage endpoints you control. For VPC deployments we can provide an IAM role/principal that enforces write-only to your bucket.
- We do not route logs or telemetry across borders unless explicitly configured and agreed as part of onboarding.

If this looks good I can turn the technical bullets into the exact contract language Neha will need. Happy to join a call if you prefer a brief walkthrough.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
